title: Nile cruise routes compared
standfirst: Nile cruises follow a handful of routes. Here they are side by side: where each starts and ends, how many nights it takes and what you see on the way. This is part of our [[up]].

sections.heading: The classic stretch
paragraphs: Almost all Nile cruises sail the stretch between Luxor and Aswan, about two hundred kilometres of river with the main temples along it: Esna, Edfu and Kom Ombo between the two cities.

sections.heading: Upstream or downstream
paragraphs: Sailing from Luxor to Aswan takes longer, because the ship sails against the current, so it is usually a four-night cruise. Sailing from Aswan to Luxor is usually three nights. The sites are the same; the order and the pace differ.

sections.heading: The dahabiya route
paragraphs: Dahabiyas usually sail between Esna and Aswan, avoiding the queue at the Esna lock and stopping at smaller sites the ships pass by.

faqs.a: Luxor to Aswan gives an extra night and a slower pace; Aswan to Luxor is shorter. Choose by the flights and the time you have.

faqs.q: Do all routes see the same temples?
faqs.a: The main temples, yes. Dahabiya routes add smaller sites.
